observation_summary: The BigFraction class fails to convert large BigInteger numerators/denominators to double/float because it performs a direct division of the primitive values, which overflow to NaN/Infinity. The fix requires a new algorithmic approach (scaling/shifting) to perform the division safely.
hypothesis: The BigFraction class lacks the necessary logic to handle large BigInteger values when converting to double or float. The current implementation directly calls doubleValue() or floatValue() on the numerator and denominator, which results in NaN or Infinity when the values exceed the range of primitive floating-point types, even if the ratio is representable. The fix requires implementing a scaling algorithm to shift the bits of the numerator and denominator into a representable range before performing the division.
prediction: The BigFraction.java source code will show that doubleValue() and floatValue() perform a simple division of numerator.doubleValue() / denominator.doubleValue() without any overflow handling or scaling logic.
experiment_rationale: The failure is clearly due to an algorithmic limitation in how the fraction is converted to a floating-point representation. The current method is insufficient for the domain of large numbers, requiring a change in the computational procedure (scaling).
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of an insufficient algorithm for handling large numbers. The conversion logic does not account for the range limitations of primitive types, leading to incorrect results (NaN). The fix involves adding a scaling step (bit shifting) to the existing method, which is a procedural/algorithmic change.
